title: When the Ganga Overflowed
subtitle: Bihar Floods 2026
description: Follow the Ganga River through eight NISAR satellite observations, from its earlier June appearance to the widespread flooding visible in September and the gradual recession during October.

chapters.title: Before the Flood
chapters.headline: A River Before the Rising Waters
chapters.narrative:
On June 20, the Ganga River appears within its earlier observed extent in our study area near Bhagalpur.

This satellite observation provides a starting point for examining how the river's appearance changes during the monsoon season.

Over the following months, the surrounding landscape will show increasingly noticeable differences.

chapters.title: The First Signs
chapters.headline: A Subtle Change Along the River
chapters.narrative:
By July 7, the river appears slightly more extensive than in the June observation.

The visible difference is relatively small, but it marks the beginning of the progression documented in this case study.

Compare the two observations to explore the earliest changes.
chapters.observation: Negligible apparent increase in water extent.

chapters.title: The River Expands
chapters.headline: The Rising Waters Become Visible
chapters.narrative:
By August 12, the satellite imagery shows a more noticeable apparent expansion of water-covered areas along the Ganga.

Compared with the June baseline, the river appears to occupy more of the surrounding landscape.

This observation marks an important stage in the developing flood story.
chapters.observation: Noticeable apparent increase in water extent.

chapters.title: Floodwaters Spread
chapters.headline: Beyond the Earlier River Extent
chapters.narrative:
On August 21, the apparent water extent has increased further.

Areas that appeared outside the main water-covered region in June now show visual patterns consistent with the expanding flood.

The progression becomes clearer when the June and August observations are compared side by side.
chapters.observation: Further apparent increase in water extent.

chapters.title: The Flood Develops
chapters.headline: A Critical Observation Before September's Peak
chapters.narrative:
On September 2, NISAR captured another observation of the Ganga near Bhagalpur.

This image helps connect the late-August observations with the extensive flooding visible later in September.

Explore this frame to examine how the river's appearance evolved during this interval.
chapters.observation: Not yet classified by the user.

chapters.title: The Flood at Its Greatest Observed Extent
chapters.headline: When the Ganga Spread Across the Floodplain
chapters.narrative:
By September 17, the Ganga appears to reach its greatest water-covered extent among the observations examined for this story.

Compared with the June baseline, the imagery shows a substantial apparent expansion into surrounding areas.

This is the central moment of our flood narrative.

Use the comparison tool to investigate how the September landscape differs from its June appearance.
chapters.observation: Largest apparent water extent among the user-examined images.

chapters.title: The Waters Begin to Retreat
chapters.headline: The River Slowly Recedes
chapters.narrative:
By October 6, the satellite imagery suggests that the water-covered area has started to decrease.

Compared with September 17, some areas appear less extensively inundated.

The flood's progression is now entering a new phase: recession.
chapters.observation: Slight apparent decrease in water extent.

chapters.title: After the Rising Waters
chapters.headline: A Landscape Emerging From the Flood
chapters.narrative:
By October 20, the apparent water extent has decreased further.

The river's appearance is moving closer to its earlier observations, although the imagery alone does not establish whether every affected area has returned to its previous condition.

Across four months, NISAR provides a visual record of the Ganga's changing appearance during the 2026 monsoon season.
chapters.observation: Further apparent decrease in water extent.

interpretation: Stages describe user-observed visual changes, not independently validated water classifications. Radar differences do not establish flood extent, depth, or the hydrological peak.
